settings.title: Do Not Wait for a No-Heat Emergency

settings.editor: Heating problems rarely get better on their own. A furnace that cycles too often, a heat pump that cannot keep up, or a system that makes new noises may already be working under extra strain.

At Lenz Heating & Cooling, we provide professional heating repair in Des Moines and across the Central Iowa area. Whether your furnace will not turn on, your heat pump is struggling, your system is blowing cool air, or certain rooms never seem warm enough, our technicians can inspect the system, explain what is happening, and recommend the repair that makes the most sense for your home.

If repair is the right call, we will tell you. If replacement is worth comparing because of system age, safety concerns, repeated repairs, or poor performance, we will explain why clearly so you can make a confident decision.

Our team at Lenz helps Des Moines homeowners get clear answers quickly. Our technicians inspect your heating system, explain what is causing the issue, and recommend practical repair options without pressure.

During sub-zero nights, early morning no-heat calls, and long cold stretches in Des Moines and Central Iowa, small heating issues can become urgent quickly. Scheduling heating repair early can help you:

settings.html:
• Restore comfort before the next cold night
  • Prevent minor issues from becoming major repairs
  • Reduce unnecessary wear on your furnace or heat pump
  • Improve efficiency and help control energy costs
  • Lower the risk of a no-heat emergency during peak winter demand
What we fix

settings.title: Types of Heating Problems We Repair

settings.editor: Different heating systems fail in different ways. A gas furnace may have ignition, burner, flame sensor, or combustion-related concerns, while a heat pump may struggle with airflow, defrost, auxiliary heat, or outdoor unit performance. Lenz Heating & Cooling repairs heating problems in gas furnaces, heat pumps, hybrid dual-fuel systems, and ductless mini-splits used for heating. Whether your system is older, newly installed, or part of a more customized comfort setup, our technicians can inspect the equipment, explain the issue, and help you understand the most practical repair option.

settings.title: No Heat or System Will Not Turn On

settings.editor:
If your heating system will not start, the issue may involve the thermostat, ignition system, control board, gas supply, safety switch, blower motor, heat pump components, or electrical connections.

Our technicians check the system carefully so you are not left guessing. Once we identify the cause, we explain the repair clearly and help you understand the safest next step.

settings.title: Cold or Lukewarm Air From the Vents

settings.editor:
A heating system that runs but does not produce enough warm air can make your home uncomfortable fast. For a gas furnace, the issue may be tied to ignition, burners, flame sensors, gas supply, airflow, or dirty components. For a heat pump, the air may feel different than furnace heat, but the system should still be able to keep your home comfortable when operating properly.

If your vents are blowing cold air, lukewarm air, or air that never seems to warm the home, professional heating repair can help identify whether the problem is simple, such as a dirty filter, or more serious, such as a failing component or system performance issue.

If some rooms feel warm while others stay cold, the problem may not be the heating equipment alone. Uneven heating can be caused by blocked vents, dirty filters, ductwork issues, weak airflow, thermostat location, zoning concerns, or a system that is struggling to distribute heat evenly.

This is common in Central Iowa homes with finished basements that never warm up, upstairs bedrooms, additions, older ductwork, or rooms far from the main system. Newer homes in areas like Waukee, Ankeny, and West Des Moines can also have comfort issues if airflow is not balanced well for the layout. Our technicians look at the full comfort picture so the repair recommendation fits your home, not just the equipment.

settings.title: Frequent Cycling or Short Heating Runs

settings.editor:
Short cycling happens when your furnace, heat pump, or heating system turns on and off too often without completing a full heating cycle. This can increase energy use, reduce comfort, and place extra wear on major components.

Common causes include restricted airflow, thermostat problems, overheating, dirty burners, flame sensor issues, heat pump performance concerns, or equipment that is not operating properly. Addressing short cycling early can help prevent larger heating system repairs.

settings.title: Loud Furnace or Heat Pump Noises

settings.editor:
Your furnace or heat pump should not bang, rattle, grind, squeal, buzz loudly, or make new sounds that continue during operation. These noises may point to loose parts, blower motor trouble, belt issues, ignition concerns, electrical problems, or worn components.

If the sound is sudden, loud, or paired with reduced heating performance, it is best to have the system inspected before running it heavily again. A small mechanical issue can become more expensive when the system keeps operating through freezing weather.

settings.title: Burning, Electrical, Musty, or Gas Odors

settings.editor:
A light dusty smell can happen when the heat first turns on for the season. But persistent burning odors, electrical smells, gas odors, or musty smells should not be ignored.

If you smell gas, leave the home and contact your gas utility or emergency services before calling for HVAC service. If you notice an electrical burning smell, shut the system off if it is safe to do so and schedule service right away.

Our technicians can inspect the heating system and help determine whether the issue is dust buildup, electrical trouble, combustion concerns, moisture, or another problem that needs repair.

If your heating system runs constantly but your home still does not feel comfortable, it may be working harder than it should. Causes can include airflow restrictions, thermostat issues, ductwork problems, dirty components, poor insulation, heat pump performance issues, or aging equipment.

During long cold stretches in Des Moines and Central Iowa, a struggling heating system can drive up energy use and still leave certain rooms uncomfortable. A professional inspection can help determine whether repair, maintenance, or another solution is the right next step.
Tell us what you're hearing or feeling and we'll work it out.

settings.html: Why it matters

settings.editor: Small heating problems can become expensive or stressful when ignored. If your system is struggling, running longer than usual, or showing warning signs, waiting can lead to more wear, higher utility costs, and a greater chance of losing heat when you need it most. Investing in timely heating repair can help improve:

image.alt: A family relaxing in a comfortable Des Moines home

settings.editor: A properly repaired heating system can deliver more consistent warmth and help reduce cold spots throughout the home.
Fixing airflow, ignition, blower, thermostat, or electrical issues can help your heating system run more efficiently and use less energy.
When problems are repaired early, your furnace or heat pump does not have to work as hard, which can reduce strain on major components.

Heating repair is not only about comfort. Gas furnaces, ignition systems, electrical components, burners, venting, and airflow all need to operate safely. If you notice gas odors, electrical smells, repeated shutdowns, or unusual combustion-related concerns, the system should be inspected before it is used heavily again.
Knowing what is wrong with your heating system and how it can be fixed helps you make confident decisions without unnecessary pressure.
